mainText: This is Dose of Good for Monday, November 16. Here are 5 good news stories. First: Wildlife carer drives 1,400 km to save a stranded baby turtle. Covered in algae, loggerhead turtle Shaggy was found floating off Esperance. Carer Letesha Heslewood drove nearly 700 km each way to take him to rehab in Bunbury. He's due to be released at Ningaloo in April. Second: Brazilian student wins gold in a world physics contest with 104 countries. Vinícius Ferreira Rodrigues, 24, placed third worldwide in the university category of Physics Cup 2026, the best result ever by a Brazilian. A former USP São Carlos student, he is now on a fully funded PhD track in the US. Third: Coal falls below half of China's electricity. In the first half of 2026, coal produced 49.7% of China's power, and CO2 emissions appear to have plateaued or fallen thanks to solar, wind, EVs and batteries. New coal plants are still being built. Fourth: Osteoporosis drug stops spinal fusion in fish. Edinburgh and Bristol scientists found an existing osteoporosis drug blocked the abnormal mineral build-up that fuses the spine in zebrafish with a faulty gene. It still needs confirming in people. Fifth: 20-year-old Argentine wins at Harvard with a device that guides blind people. Martín Pulitano and his team won HackHarvard, out of 500+ participants, with FEEL: a US$70 prototype that uses AI and touch to signal what's ahead and alongside. They now want blind people to test it. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
